scope: Synthetic Engine discovery, parser subprocesses, chunks and SQLite FTS; semantic disabled.
source_sha256_method: SHA256 of sorted src/**/*.py relative POSIX paths followed by raw file bytes, exactly scripts/bench_indexing.py source_hash.

method.file_events: explicit complete reconciliation each phase; no idle scheduler or OS notification delay
method.verification: all indexed chunk text and locators equal baseline extraction+chunking; each file head/tail FTS queries; obsolete head absent after edit
method.memory: 25ms sampled Engine plus descendant RSS, including limit helpers; excludes DSH Web/Node/MCP and fixture generation
method.cpu: sampled cumulative parent+child CPU; exited child tail can be undercounted
method.sql: trace-instrumented operation times; durable COMMIT + outer SAVEPOINT RELEASE, schema initialization excluded
method.fixed: both versions 1024MiB process-tree ceiling, 1 parser, 512MiB worker, 25 percent worker CPU, 0 fixed delay
method.cache: no OS disk-cache eviction; initial worker/import cold, later reuse or retirement follows product idle policy; one run per variant
method.final_comparison: Baseline variants retained from first run; both current variants rerun after transaction fix on the identical generated corpus and baseline oracle.
method.verification_interpretation: obsolete_keyword_absent false before the modified phase means not applicable; every phase checks complete text and locators. query_count counts timed head/tail queries only; modified phase also checks 384 obsolete head queries.
method.process_count: Includes parser subprocesses and Windows resource limit helper processes; 12 descendants does not mean 12 parsers.
method.stage_timing: Internal parse times sum individual concurrent tasks, so stages must not be summed into elapsed wall time.
method.cpu_precision: 25ms is the requested polling interval, not guaranteed scheduler cadence; counters may miss the exited-process tail.

initial_candidate_counterexample.conclusion: Initial fixed-resource first-index time regressed 47.17%; later batch transaction fix reduced this to 3.05%, not a demonstrated same-resource first-index speedup.
initial_candidate_counterexample.diagnostic_evidence: 32-file cProfile pointed at SQLite writes. Removing the single-worker executor did not resolve the regression. FTS5 3.40.1 xSavepoint/xRelease flush pending index data; safe batch-level rollback and fewer nested savepoints were then tested by the parent task.

extractor_microbenchmark.scope: synthetic extractor-only warm runs; no user files, subprocess startup, index writes, or semantic inference
extractor_microbenchmark.memory_metric: separate tracemalloc run; Python allocation peak, not RSS

limitations: 384 synthetic files, 44.56MiB; not hundreds of GB of real documents.
One run per variant, no randomized order or confidence interval; OS disk cache not evicted.
32GiB host; not a validation on a physical 8GiB host or the user remote machine.
RSS covers Engine and descendants only, excluding DSH Web, Node, MCP, models and fixture generation.
Measurements use explicit complete reconciliation, not file notifications, background idle scheduling or concurrent search load.
SQL tracing and process sampling add overhead. Sampled CPU and RSS can undercount short lived activity.
Oracle is baseline extraction and chunking, proving compatibility on these fixtures, not independent proof every source format is parsed completely.
Extractor-only warm medians and tracemalloc allocation peaks are not service end-to-end speedups or process RSS.
